描述_EN: at this site material was discovered at a buddhist shrine abandoned in the 4rd or 5th century ad. the site is part of an area of central asia we now call the silk road, a series of overland trade routes that crossed asia, from china to europe. whilst silk textiles travelled west from china, buddhism entered china from india in this way. camels and horses were used as pack animals and merchants passed the goods from oasis to oasis. the victoria and albert museum has around 700 ancient and medieval textiles recovered by stein at the beginning of the twentieth century. the most notable item traded was silk. the silk road was also important for the exchange of ideas. they were recovered from the site of miran on the eastern verge of the taklamakan desert. they form the remains of unfinished cut flowers. some are silk while others are made from the wool of a variety of different animals. these textile fragments were brought back from central asia by the explorer and archaeologist sir marc aurel stein (1862-1943). these fragments are of monochrome, plain woven, buff silk.
描述_ZN: 该遗址的材料是在公元4、5世纪废弃的佛教圣地发现的。 该遗址是中亚地区的一部分，我们现在称之为丝绸之路，这是一系列横跨亚洲的陆上贸易路线，从中国到欧洲。 年，当丝织品从中国西行时，佛教通过这种方式从印度进入中国。 年，骆驼和马被用作驮运动物，商人们在绿洲之间传递货物。 年，维多利亚和阿尔伯特博物馆有大约700件古代和中世纪的纺织品，是斯坦在20世纪初找到的。 年，最引人注目的贸易项目是丝绸。 年：丝绸之路对于思想的交流也很重要。 它们是在塔克拉玛干沙漠东部边缘的Miran遗址中发现的。 它们形成了未完成的切花的遗迹。 有些是丝绸，有些则是由各种不同动物的羊毛制成。 这些纺织品碎片是由探险家和考古学家Marc Aurel Stein先生（1862-1943）从亚洲中部带回的。 这些碎片是单色的，平织的，水色的丝绸。
